title: Observability Core Principles, RED & USE Frameworks & SLI Telemetry
summary: Master cloud-native observability principles: distinguishing telemetry signals (metrics, logs, traces), implementing the RED (Rate, Errors, Duration) framework for request-driven services, implementing the USE (Utilization, Saturation, Errors) framework for infrastructure resources, and defining precise Service Level Indicators (SLIs).
learningObjectives: Contrast the trade-offs, storage costs, and cardinality characteristics of metrics, structured logs, and distributed traces.
Formulate RED metrics (Rate, Errors, Duration) to evaluate microservice health, throughput, and error budgets.
Formulate USE metrics (Utilization, Saturation, Errors) to identify infrastructure bottlenecks across CPU, memory, and storage.

curriculumModules.title: Telemetry Foundations: The Three Pillars & Cardinality Management
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Observability is built upon three foundational signals: metrics (aggregated numerical time-series), logs (timestamped structured events), and traces (causally connected spans traversing microservices). High-cardinality label explosion (e.g. user IDs or GUIDs in Prometheus metric labels) severely degrades TSDB performance and must be strictly governed.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Preserve low-cardinality static dimensions in metric labels (cluster, region, service, statusCode) while offloading high-cardinality identifiers (userId, traceId, orderGuid) into structured log fields or distributed trace span attributes.

curriculumModules.title: RED & USE Observability Frameworks & SLI Formulation
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Tom Wilkie's RED Method models request-driven services: Rate (requests/sec), Errors (failed requests/sec), and Duration (latency distribution). Brendan Gregg's USE Method models resource bottlenecks: Utilization (percentage of time resource was busy), Saturation (extra work queued), and Errors (hardware/system error counts). These frameworks define actionable Service Level Indicators (SLIs).
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Standardize SLI dashboards across engineering squads: instrument HTTP/gRPC ingress with RED metrics for user satisfaction and host nodes with USE metrics for capacity planning and autoscaling.

labs.title: Formulating RED Metrics & SLI Telemetry Specifications
labs.scenario: Design request-driven microservice observability: author an SLI telemetry specification in /obs/red-telemetry.json defining RED metrics for checkout-service (rateMetric: http_requests_total, errorFilter: status=~"5..", and durationMetric: http_request_duration_seconds_bucket). Deploy a ConfigMap named checkout-telemetry-config in namespace monitoring embedding this telemetry contract.
labs.productionContext: Explicit RED telemetry definitions ensure consistent dashboarding, alerting, and automated SLO burn rate evaluation across distributed microservice architectures.
objectives: Create and apply ConfigMap checkout-telemetry-config in namespace monitoring.
Verify telemetry config contains rate and duration metrics.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: checkout-telemetry-config
  namespace: monitoring
data:
  red-telemetry.json: |
    {
      "service": "checkout-service",
      "framework": "RED",
      "rateMetric": "http_requests_total",
      "errorFilter": "status=~\"5..\"",
      "durationMetric": "http_request_duration_seconds_bucket"
    }

steps.instruction: Save the RED JSON schema to /obs/red-telemetry.json.

labs.title: Auditing Cluster Infrastructure Health via the USE Framework
labs.scenario: Audit cluster infrastructure resource bottlenecks using USE metrics: execute promql queries to inspect node CPU Utilization (node_cpu_utilization), memory Saturation (node_memory_saturation), and filesystem Errors (node_filesystem_errors_total), saving the audit report to /obs/use-audit.txt.
labs.productionContext: The USE method provides immediate triage during node pressure incidents by systematically isolating whether hardware or kernel subsystems are exhausted, saturated with queuing, or failing with errors.
objectives: Execute promql query for node CPU utilization.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which metrics framework is specifically designed for observing request-driven microservices, and what three signals does it capture?
options: The USE framework: Utilization, Saturation, and Errors.
The RED framework: Rate (requests/sec), Errors (failed requests/sec), and Duration (latency distribution).
The DORA framework: Deployment Frequency, Lead Time, Change Fail Rate, and Time to Restore.
The ACID framework: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Tom Wilkie's RED method measures user-facing request performance: Rate (traffic volume), Errors (failure rate), and Duration (latency). The USE framework is used for infrastructure resources.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is metric cardinality explosion in a Prometheus time-series database, and what causes it?
options: It occurs when disk space is exhausted due to storing metrics for more than 30 days.

It occurs when a metric label contains unbounded, unique values (such as user IDs, request UUIDs, or timestamps), generating millions of distinct time-series and causing Prometheus to exhaust memory and crash.
It occurs when too many Pods are scraped simultaneously via HTTP/2.
It occurs when PromQL queries use sum() instead of avg().
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Cardinality equals the total number of unique time-series generated by label combinations. Unbounded values like user IDs or UUIDs multiply timeseries exponentially, leading to severe memory exhaustion (OOM).
